To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Benito Juárez International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=mmmx

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from Mexico’s Servicio Meteorológico Nacional indicate a daytime maximum of 24–26°C for Mexico City on September 6 amid partly to mostly cloudy skies, strong afternoon convection, and localized heavy rainfall with hail potential. High-elevation cooling at roughly 2,240 meters, combined with persistent cloud cover and evaporative cooling from precipitation, is keeping the implied probability highest for a 24°C peak, followed closely by 23°C and 25°C. Model consensus shows limited upside above 26°C given the saturated atmosphere and typical September rainy-season patterns, while downside risk to 22°C or below remains low unless rainfall intensifies earlier than expected. Updated model runs and official observations throughout the day will determine final resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Trader consensus for Panama City’s September 6 maximum centers on 30–32 °C because official forecasts and ensemble guidance show a narrow range around 30–31 °C amid typical wet-season convection.** Afternoon thunderstorms, driven by the Intertropical Convergence Zone and high Caribbean moisture, increase cloud cover and evaporative cooling that frequently caps daytime peaks near 30–31 °C; however, brief breaks in convection or slightly stronger insolation can allow brief excursions to 32 °C. Model runs exhibit modest spread in timing and intensity of showers, keeping the 30 °C, 31 °C, and 32 °C bins closely matched while rendering 33 °C or higher unlikely under current steering patterns and sea-surface temperatures. Updated National Meteorological Service guidance and satellite-derived instability indices will refine the final observed high before market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Persistent southerly flow and widespread rain are keeping maximum temperatures tightly constrained around 9–11 °C for Wellington on 7 September.** Official guidance from MetService-aligned models and international ensembles shows a cool, moist airmass advected behind a front, with southeast winds of 20–25 kt suppressing daytime warming despite partial clearing later in the day. Traders therefore cluster on the 10 °C and 11 °C contracts because small shifts in timing of clearing or wind direction could tip the peak by 1 °C, while probabilities above 12 °C remain low given the established cool advection. Updated model runs and MetService briefings tomorrow morning will be the next key catalysts.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Shanghai Pudong International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zspd

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

**Consensus short-range forecasts from multiple models place Chengdu’s September 7 maximum near 33–34 °C under increasing cloud cover and a chance of showers.** 

Official guidance shows mostly cloudy skies with light northeast winds and a 30–50 % probability of scattered rain or thunderstorms by afternoon, which reduces surface heating relative to the clearer conditions of September 5–6. This cloud-radiative effect, combined with modest moisture advection into the Sichuan Basin, caps daytime temperatures below recent peaks while still exceeding the September climatological average. Traders therefore assign the highest implied probabilities to the 33 °C and 34 °C bins, reflecting the narrow but non-negligible uncertainty in exact timing and intensity of any showers. Final resolution will depend on the official 24-hour maximum recorded by the Chengdu meteorological station.

High temperatures are projected to peak near 12–13°C, well below the long-term September 7 average of 18°C, as a cooler air mass dominates following recent unsettled weather. These conditions support the market’s leading outcomes at 12°C and 13°C, which together exceed 80% implied probability. Minor model variations in cloud cover or timing of any showers could shift the exact maximum by 1°C, but consensus remains tight ahead of tomorrow’s official observations.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon activity, reinforced by broad low-level convergence and high moisture, is the main driver keeping Manila's September 7 daytime maximum near 29–30 °C according to the latest GFS and ECMWF guidance. Widespread cloud cover and frequent showers or thunderstorms are expected to limit solar heating, with model consensus favoring a peak around 28–30 °C rather than the higher values sometimes seen in clearer conditions. Recent PAGASA impact-based outlooks highlight continued heavy rain potential through early September, consistent with climatological norms for the peak monsoon period when average highs hover near 29 °C. Traders appear to weigh the possibility of brief afternoon clearing that could allow a 30–31 °C spike against the more probable suppressed maxima, with updated model runs and official PAGASA bulletins the next key inputs likely to refine these implied probabilities.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Austin-Bergstrom International Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=kaus

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This places the most probable outcome in the 98-99°F bin favored by traders at 49.5 percent implied probability, with the 100-101°F range at 24 percent reflecting residual uncertainty in afternoon mixing and cloud cover. Above-average warmth relative to the 1991-2020 September 7 mean of 93°F stems from persistent southerly advection and elevated dew points that sustain heat without widespread convection. Low precipitation chances under 10 percent further support limited cooling, while model consensus leaves only modest upside risk for 102°F or higher. Updated guidance through the evening of September 6 will refine the exact maximum before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: A polar air mass and associated cold front have driven trader focus toward a narrow 12–15°C range for São Paulo’s September 7 maximum, far below the early-September climatological average near 24°C. Persistent southeast winds, high pressure, and widespread low cloud cover are limiting daytime solar heating while light rain or drizzle adds evaporative cooling, with official guidance from Climatempo and INMET-aligned models converging on daytime peaks of 12–15°C. The tight clustering of implied probabilities around 13–14°C reflects model consensus on these conditions, tempered by remaining uncertainty in exact cloud timing and any urban heat-island modulation at the official measurement site. Updated runs from regional and global ensembles overnight will provide the final calibration before the market resolves.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Recent model consensus for Panama City, Panama, points to a daily maximum near 31–32°C on September 7, with afternoon convection and high humidity the main reasons trader probabilities cluster tightly around those two outcomes.** In the peak of the rainy season, the Intertropical Convergence Zone sustains deep moisture and widespread instability; solar heating builds instability through the morning, but scattered to numerous thunderstorms typically develop by early afternoon. These storms increase cloud cover, enhance evaporative cooling, and reduce net insolation, often capping the temperature 1–2°C below what clear-sky radiative heating would produce. Sea-breeze circulation from the Pacific and Caribbean further modulates boundary-layer moisture and wind, while small differences in model timing of convective initiation or total cloud fraction create the narrow spread between 31°C and 32°C. With resolution based on official daily maximum observations, any shift in the latest ECMWF or GFS runs regarding precipitation onset will likely move the market most directly.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 8 Sep '26.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from models like ECMWF and GFS indicate a peak temperature in Milan on September 8 near 32–33°C, driven by a ridge of high pressure promoting southerly warm air advection and initially clear skies with light winds. Afternoon instability may trigger isolated thunderstorms, introducing minor cooling potential that narrows the range between 31°C and 33°C outcomes. Market-implied odds reflect this tight consensus, with traders weighting historical September baselines around 25–27°C and urban heat island effects that can add 1–2°C in the city center. Key variables include exact cloud timing and boundary layer mixing, with updated model runs expected to refine probabilities before resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Helsinki Vantaa Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 8 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=efhk

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent official forecasts for Helsinki on September 8 point to a daytime maximum of 17–18 °C, aligning closely with the market’s leading outcomes.** Multiple sources, including the Finnish Meteorological Institute (Ilmatieteen laitos), Foreca, and yr.no, indicate highs near 18 °C or 17 °C under mostly cloudy skies with light southerly winds and a modest chance of rain. These conditions favor mild maritime air rather than strong warming or cooling.

This setup sits slightly above the 1991–2020 climatological average high of 16.7 °C for the date, reflecting typical early-September variability without extreme anomalies. Model consensus shows limited spread, with little support for 19 °C or higher or sub-16 °C readings, which explains the steep drop-off in implied probabilities beyond the top two bins. Traders appear to be weighting the latest model runs and regional guidance that keep temperatures in the narrow 17–18 °C window, with any further forecast updates from the Finnish Meteorological Institute or ECMWF likely to refine these odds ahead of resolution.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.
